title: Een huis huren
subtitle: Renting a place
intro: In this lesson you learn to read a Dutch rental ad and to call about it. You can ask what the rent and the deposit are, what is included in the price, and when you can come and have a look. You also practise polite indirect questions with of, which make you sound natural on the phone.

grammar.title: Yes/no questions about the rental conditions
grammar.explanation: In a yes/no question the verb comes first and the subject comes after it: **Is het appartement nog beschikbaar?** The rest of the sentence stays the same. With a question word like **hoeveel** the order is question word + verb + subject: **Hoeveel is de borg?**

rows: De huur is 950 euro per maand.

examples.nl: Zijn de servicekosten inclusief of exclusief?
examples.en: Are the service charges included or not?

grammar.tip: Dutch and English do the same thing here: het appartement is -> is het appartement?

grammar.title: Indirect questions with of and question words
grammar.explanation: After a polite opening such as **Weet u...?** or **Kunt u zeggen...?** you use **of** for a yes/no question, or a question word (**wanneer, hoe, wat, waar**). Then the subject comes first and the verb goes to the end: **Weet u of het appartement nog vrij is?** With a modal verb the infinitive comes last: **Kunt u zeggen wanneer ik kan komen kijken?**

rows: Weet u of het appartement vrij is?
Kunt u zeggen wanneer ik kan komen?
Mag ik vragen hoeveel de huur is?

examples.nl: Weet u of het appartement nog vrij is?
examples.en: Do you know whether the apartment is still available?

examples.nl: Kunt u zeggen wanneer ik kan komen kijken?
examples.en: Can you tell me when I can come and have a look?

examples.nl: Mag ik vragen hoeveel de servicekosten zijn?
examples.en: May I ask how much the service charges are?

grammar.tip: of means 'whether' here. Think: Weet u of ... + subject + verb at the end.

grammar.title: Rents, numbers and per maand
grammar.explanation: Amounts under 1000 are written as one word: **negenhonderdvijftig**. For 1100–1999 you often say **elfhonderd**, **twaalfhonderd**, ... **veertienhonderdvijftig**. **euro** does not get an -s after a number. Use **per maand**, **per week**, **per jaar**. **inclusief** and **exclusief** stand before the thing they talk about: **inclusief servicekosten**.

examples.nl: De huur is negenhonderdvijftig euro per maand.
examples.en: The rent is 950 euros a month.

examples.nl: De huur is veertienhonderdvijftig euro exclusief servicekosten.
examples.en: The rent is 1450 euros excluding service charges.

examples.nl: Het appartement is zestig vierkante meter.
examples.en: The apartment is sixty square metres.

grammar.tip: Say euro, not euro's: twee euro, 950 euro, twintig euro.

dialogue.title: Ik bel over uw advertentie
dialogue.setting: Sanne calls a landlord about an ad and then asks about the apartment.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Goedemiddag, u spreekt met Sanne Visser. Ik bel over uw advertentie. Is het appartement nog beschikbaar?
lines.en: Good afternoon, this is Sanne Visser. I'm calling about your ad. Is the apartment still available?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: Ja, het is nog vrij. Het is op de tweede verdieping.
lines.en: Yes, it is still free. It is on the second floor.

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: Het is ongemeubileerd. De huur is 950 euro per maand, exclusief de servicekosten.
lines.en: It is unfurnished. The rent is 950 euros a month, excluding the service charges.

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: De borg is één maand huur. Wilt u alleen wonen?
lines.en: The deposit is one month's rent. Do you want to live alone?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ja, ik wil alleen wonen. Is er een lift?
lines.en: Yes, I want to live alone. Is there a lift?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: Ja, er is een lift. De buurt is rustig en het centrum is dichtbij.
lines.en: Yes, there is a lift. The neighbourhood is quiet and the centre is nearby.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Hoeveel vierkante meter is het appartement?
lines.en: How many square metres is the apartment?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: Zestig vierkante meter. Wanneer wilt u komen kijken?
lines.en: Sixty square metres. When would you like to come and have a look?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Kan ik morgen om vier uur komen kijken?
lines.en: Can I come and have a look tomorrow at four o'clock?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Boer
lines.nl: Dat is goed. Dan stuur ik u het contract alvast.
lines.en: That's fine. Then I will send you the contract in advance.

Hallo, met Sanne Visser. Ik bel over uw advertentie. Is het appartement nog vrij?

mistakes.explain: Appartement is a het-word: "het appartement".

mistakes.pattern: Uses voor instead of over about the ad (Ik bel voor uw advertentie.)
mistakes.explain: Call about an ad is "Ik bel over uw advertentie".

say.nl: Ja, het is nog beschikbaar. Het is op de eerste verdieping, 55 vierkante meter. De huur is 950 euro per maand.
say.en: Yes, it is still available. It is on the first floor, 55 square metres. The rent is 950 euros a month.

mistakes.explain: Borg is a de-word: "de borg".

mistakes.explain: Servicekosten take de, but gas, water en licht take no article here: "Zijn gas, water en licht inclusief?"

culture.title: Woningnood: snel reageren en alles op papier
culture.text: In large Dutch cities there are far fewer rentals than people looking for one, so a single ad can get dozens of reactions in a day. Call or email the same day and have your documents ready. Always ask for a written contract and check what is included, because service costs, gas, water and light are often separate. Never pay a deposit without a contract and a receipt.

summary: Ask about the huur, the borg and the servicekosten before you visit.
Yes/no questions start with the verb: Is het appartement nog beschikbaar?
Indirect questions use of or a question word, with the verbs at the end: Weet u of het nog vrij is?
Say amounts like negenhonderdvijftig euro per maand; euro does not take -s.
Good rentals go fast: react the same day and ask for a written contract.
